test_title: RRB Technician Grade III Official Paper (Held On: 29 Dec, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Select the correct statement.

options.text: When a girl is born, the ovaries already contain thousands of immature eggs.
Many eggs are produced every month by the ovary.
The fallopian tube is also known as womb.

solution:
The correct answer is __**1) When a girl is born, the ovaries already contain thousands of immature eggs.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Females are born with a finite number of eggs. **At birth, a female's ovaries contain approximately 1-2 million immature eggs (oocytes).**
 
• These eggs remain dormant until puberty, when they begin to mature during the menstrual cycle.
 
• Throughout a woman's reproductive life, only about 400-500 eggs will mature and be released during ovulation.
 
• By the time of puberty, the number of eggs decreases to about 300,000 to 400,000.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Oogenesis**: The process of egg formation in females is known as oogenesis. It begins before birth and is completed only if fertilization occurs.
 
• **Follicles**: Each immature egg is contained within a structure called a follicle. During the menstrual cycle, follicles grow and mature, preparing for the release of an egg.
 
• **Menstrual Cycle**: The cycle typically lasts about 28 days, during which an egg matures and is released from the ovary (ovulation). If the egg is not fertilized, it is shed during menstruation.
 
• **Hormonal Regulation**: The maturation and release of eggs are regulated by hormones such as Follicle Stimulating Hormone (FSH) and Luteinizing Hormone (LH).
